facts.statement: Leonerasaurus taquetrensis was named by Diego Pol, Alberto Garrido, and Ignacio A. Cerda in 2011.
facts.quote: Currently, there is only one species known, named L. taquetrensis by Diego Pol, Alberto Garrido and Ignacio A. Cerda in 2011.

facts.statement: The fossil of an incomplete subadult Leonerasaurus was found in the Early Jurassic Las Leoneras Formation in Argentina.
facts.quote: The fossil, an incomplete subadult individual, was found in the Las Leoneras Formation in Argentina. This formation is probably Early Jurassic in age.

facts.statement: The Las Leoneras Formation is interpreted as dating from the Pliensbachian to Toarcian or late Sinemurian to Toarcian stages of the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: This formation is probably early Jurassic in age, interpreted as Pliensbachian to Toarcian or late Sinemurian to Toarcian.

facts.statement: Leonerasaurus taquetrensis lived approximately 190 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Leonerasaurus taquetrensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Leonerasaurus de dinosaurio sauropodomorfo anquisáurido que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 190 millones de años, durante el Sinemuriense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Leonerasaurus was a small non-sauropod sauropodomorph that displayed an unusual mix of primitive and advanced traits.
facts.quote: Leonerasaurus was a small non-sauropod sauropodomorph, showing an unusual combination of basal and derived characters.

facts.statement: Leonerasaurus measured approximately 2.40 meters in length, 1 meter in height, and weighed about 70 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was only 2.40 meters long, 1 m high and weighing about 70 kg.

facts.statement: The species is known from a single incomplete individual consisting of parts of the skull, teeth, vertebrae, hip and shoulder girdles, and limb bones.
facts.quote: Leonerasaurus taquetrensis is known from one incomplete individual. Parts of a dentary and some teeth, neck and trunk vertebrae, a sacrum, parts of the pectoral (shoulder) and pelvis (hip) girdle as well as several limb bones were found.

facts.statement: The front teeth of Leonerasaurus were spoon-shaped with a convex outer surface and concave inner surface, resembling those of basal sauropods.
facts.quote: The anterior teeth are spoon-shaped, with the outer surface convex (bulging out), the inner one concave (hollowed out), again resembling basal sauropods.

facts.statement: At least 15 teeth were present on one side of the lower jaw, based on 13 found fragments and two empty sockets.
facts.quote: On the dentary, 13 teeth or tooth fragments were found. There are two empty alveoli, so that the total tooth count on one side was at least 15.

facts.statement: The teeth and tooth sockets were angled forward by approximately 60 degrees, a feature similar to eusauropods and juvenile Mussaurus.
facts.quote: The teeth and alveoli are angled forward (procumbent) by ~60°, similar to eusauropods, but also to juveniles of Mussaurus.

facts.statement: The sacrum, made of four fused vertebrae, is nearly complete, but no tail bones were recovered.
facts.quote: The sacrum (fused vertebrae that form the core of the hip), consisting of four vertebrae, is nearly complete, but no bones of the tail was recovered.

facts.statement: Leonerasaurus is classified as a basal genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur.
facts.quote: Leonerasaurus is a basal genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur.

facts.statement: Research suggests Leonerasaurus belongs to the Anchisauria, appearing as the closest relative to the group containing sauropods and Melanorosaurus.
facts.quote: Leonerasaurus appears to be belong into the Anchisauria, as the closest sister taxon to the group sauropods (following Yates) + Melanorosaurus (M. is seen as a sauropod by some researchers).

facts.statement: Leonerasaurus is classified within the unranked group Anchisauria.
facts.quote: unranked_genus: Anchisauria

facts.statement: It is debated whether Leonerasaurus lived in the Late Triassic, as the lower age limit of the Las Leoneras Formation is not well-defined.
facts.quote: However, a Late Triassic affinity cannot be rules out, because the lower constraint of the formation is not well-defined.

facts.statement: The unique combination of traits in Leonerasaurus suggests a high degree of convergent evolution in early sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: This indicates that the evolution of early sauropodomorphs witnessed a great degree of convergent evolution.

facts.statement: Leonerasaurus was a small animal reaching only 2.40 meters in length, 1 meter in height, and weighing approximately 70 kilograms.
facts.quote: llegaba a medir solo 2,40 metros de largo, 1 de alto y a pesar cerca de 70 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The only part of the skull found was the anterior portion of the right dentary bone.
facts.quote: Del cráneo solamente se halló la parte anterior del dentario derecho.

facts.statement: The front teeth were spoon-shaped with a convex outer surface and a concave inner surface, similar to sauropods.
facts.quote: Los dientes anteriores eran en forma de cuchara, con la superficie exterior convexa (prominencia), la interior cóncava (ahuecado), similar a la de los saurópodos.

facts.statement: The sacrum, consisting of four fused vertebrae forming the center of the pelvis, is nearly complete, but no tail bones were discovered.
facts.quote: El sacro, las vértebras fusionadas que forman el centro de la cadera, consistente de cuatro vértebras, está casi completo, pero no se descubrieron huesos de la cola.

facts.statement: Only one individual is known, named L. taquetrensis by Diego Pol, Alberto Garrido, and Ignacio A. Cerda in 2011.
facts.quote: Actualmente, solamente se conoce un individuo, nombrado L. taquetrensis por Diego Pol, Alberto Garrido y Ignacio A. Cerda en 2011.

facts.statement: Fossils of an incomplete juvenile individual were found in the Las Leoneras Formation in Argentina.
facts.quote: Los fósiles encontrados, de un individuo juvenil incompleto, fueron hallados en la formación Las Leoneras en Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils were found near Cañadón Las Leoneras, southeast of Sierra de Taquetrén, in Chubut province, central Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los fósiles asignados a Leonerasaurus fueron encontrados cerca de Cañadón Las Leoneras (un afluente en la margen izquierda del río Chubut), al sureste de Sierra de Taquetrén, provincia de Chubut, en el centro de la Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: The formation dates to the early Jurassic, interpreted as the Pliensbachian to Toarcian or late Sinemurian to Toarcian periods.
facts.quote: Esta formación data probablemente de principios del Jurásico, interpretado como el período desde el Pliensbachiano al Toarciano o finales del Sinemuriano a Toarciano.

facts.statement: Leonerasaurus lived between 192.9 and 184.2 million years ago during the Pliensbachian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Pliensbachian to Pliensbachian (192.9 to 184.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Leonerasaurus appears to belong to Anchisauria as a sister taxon to sauropods according to Yates' definition, though Melanorosaurus is considered a sauropod by some researchers.
facts.quote: Leonerasaurus parece pertenecer a los Anchisauria, como el taxón hermano a los saurópodos, según la definición de Yates junto con Melanorosaurus, aunque este último es visto como un saurópodo por algunos investigadores.

facts.statement: Leonerasaurus was a small non-sauropod sauropodomorph showing an unusual combination of basal and derived characteristics.
facts.quote: Leonerasaurus era un pequeño sauropodomorfo no saurópodo, mostrando una inusual combinación de características basales y derivadas.

facts.statement: It is suggested that the evolution of primitive sauropodomorphs involved significant convergent evolution among diverse lineages.
facts.quote: Esto indica que la evolución de los sauropodomorfos primitivos tuvo mucho de evolución convergente entre diversos linajes.

rejected.statement: The neck is nearly complete with nine vertebrae, which were found articulated with the first five complete trunk vertebrae.
rejected.quote: The neck of Leonerasaurus is known almost completely, only the atlas is lost. The nine remaining cervicals were found articulated with the first five complete dorsal (trunk) vertebrae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'were found articulated with the first five complete'

rejected.statement: Thirteen teeth or fragments were found in the dentary, suggesting a total count of at least 15 teeth.
rejected.quote: En el dentario, 13 dientes o fragmentos de los mismos fueron hallados.
